name: Engineering Hub
tagline: Specs, RFCs, ADRs, a sprint board and runbooks as plain files, right beside your code and your coding agent.
description:
An engineering team's workspace, shown through a worked example: Atlas API, the public geocoding and places API of a fictional company, run by a six-person platform team in the middle of a sprint. They are shipping rate limiting and recovering from a latency incident, so every page and view already has something real in it.

Specs come first: an architecture overview with diagrams and SLOs, an RFC for rate limiting and a glossary whose terms other pages link to directly. A Tickets database runs the sprint as a board, a current-sprint list, a bug queue and a points chart, and an ADR log records why things are the way they are. Runbooks cover deploys, incident response, on-call and the changelog, with a filled-in blameless postmortem and blank templates for design docs, ADRs and postmortems.

Three AI recipes write the daily standup, draft ADRs and turn an incident timeline into a postmortem. Two tools come with it: a changelog drafter that turns done tickets into release notes, and an incident log that keeps a timestamped timeline while you fight the fire. Point Claude Code or Cursor at the folder and they read the same specs you do.
overview: Engineering team workspace: architecture overview, RFCs and a linked glossary, a sprint ticket board with a changelog view, an ADR log, deploy and incident runbooks, a sample postmortem and design-doc templates.
